md_description: This workflow transforms traditional medicinal plant material into purified bioactive-compound fractions, structural identifications, and cellular bioactivity readouts. It combines chromatographic isolation, spectroscopic characterization, and cell-based antioxidant and anti-inflammatory assays to produce integrated derived results that can support standardized nutraceutical development and health-benefit claims.

traditional_medicinal_plant_material.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the collected plant biomass: what plant it is, where it came from, what part was collected, and the collection context needed to trace starting material provenance. I excluded any processing fields such as drying, grinding, extraction, chromatography, spectroscopy, assay conditions, or derived analytical outputs because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating generic identifiers if they were likely to be generated elsewhere at the root, and focused on plant-material-specific provenance and biological source details that are unique to this starting Entity.

md_schema.descr: Accepted botanical name of the medicinal plant material at collection, using genus_species format when known (for example, 'Azadirachta indica'). Record the taxon identity of the starting biomass, not the processed sample.
Local or common name used to refer to the medicinal plant material at collection (for example, 'neem', 'holy basil'). Record as reported by the collector or source documentation.
Plant anatomical part used as the starting biological material, recorded at collection time. Examples include leaf, root, stem, bark, flower, seed, whole_plant.

Geographic collection origin of the plant biomass, recorded as the source locality for provenance tracing. Use a recognizable place name, site code, or coordinates if available (for example, 'Kerala, India' or '12.97N 77.59E').
Date when the medicinal plant material was collected from the field or source repository, in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD if exact date is known. This is the provenance date for the starting biomass.
How the starting plant biomass was obtained at the source, such as wild_collected, cultivated, purchased, or herbarium_source. Record the provenance pathway, not later preparation steps.
Herbarium or voucher identifier assigned to the source plant specimen, if a voucher was deposited. Use a stable string identifier such as 'VCH-2024-017'.
Botanical family of the collected medicinal plant, recorded as an intrinsic taxonomic classification for the source biomass (for example, 'Lamiaceae').
Whether the source plant biomass was obtained from wild or cultivated material at the time of collection. This describes origin, not processing.
Initial physical condition of the collected biomass before any cleaning, drying, or grinding. Use a categorical descriptor such as fresh or partially_dried when relevant.

dry_clean_grind_plants.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only operation parameters describing how the plant biomass was cleaned, dried, and milled into homogenized feedstock. I focused on actionable protocol details: cleaning method, drying conditions, grinding/milling settings, target particle size, batch handling, and a simple in-process quality indicator. I excluded source-material provenance fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded extraction, chromatography, or downstream analytical outputs because they are outside this process’s scope. I also avoided duplicating any root-level identifiers already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Cleaning approach applied to the collected plant material before drying and milling, such as water_rinse, solvent_wipe, manual_sorting, or none. Record the method actually used on the biomass entering this process.

Drying approach used to prepare the plant material, recorded at the process step. Examples include air_dry, oven_dry, lyophilize, or shade_dry. This describes how moisture was removed before grinding.
Temperature used during drying, in degrees Celsius, measured or set during the drying phase of this process. Typical values may range from ambient temperature to about 80 C depending on method.

Total drying time for the plant material, in hours, measured from start to completion of the drying phase. Typical values range from a few hours to several days depending on drying method and biomass load.
Grinding or milling approach used to homogenize the dried plant material, such as mortar_and_pestle, blade_mill, ball_mill, or cryomill. Record the method used to produce extraction feedstock.
Duration of the grinding or milling step, in minutes, measured for the homogenization operation. Typical values range from less than 1 minute to several tens of minutes depending on equipment.

Target or achieved particle size after milling, in micrometers, measured for the homogenized plant powder prior to extraction. Typical values range from about 50 to 2000 micrometer depending on downstream extraction needs.
Sieve mesh size used to standardize the milled plant powder, recorded as the nominal sieve designation or numeric mesh value if applied. Use this only if sieving was part of homogenization.

Internal batch identifier for the cleaned, dried, and ground material prepared in this process, using a stable string such as 'PREP-001'. This identifies the preparation lot, not the biological source specimen.
Simple quality indicator for the resulting extraction feedstock after cleaning, drying, and milling, such as uniform, partially_uniform, or heterogeneous, assessed at process completion.

prepared_plant_powder.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared plant powder itself: what material it is, its physical form, condition, and provenance from the preparation step. I emphasized state descriptors needed to reuse the material for extraction and chromatography, such as moisture/appearance and particle-size/homogeneity summaries. I excluded the upstream process settings for cleaning, drying, and grinding because those belong to the dry_clean_grind_plants Process node, and I excluded extraction/chromatography outputs because those are downstream. I also avoided repeating source-plant identifiers already established at the root Entity node.

md_schema.descr: Name or internal label for the prepared plant powder as a reusable material entity, such as 'prepared leaf powder' or a lab inventory label. This identifies the processed biomass aliquot ready for extraction.

Plant part from which this powder was prepared, carried forward as an intrinsic description of the material source (for example, leaf, root, bark). Record the source part of the powder rather than the original whole plant.
Physical form of the material after preparation, recorded as a categorical description of the entity state. Use this to document that the material is powdered and homogenized for extraction.
Observed or specified particle-size range of the prepared powder, in micrometers, measured or estimated after grinding and any sieving. Typical values may span roughly 50 to 2000 micrometer.
Qualitative moisture state of the prepared powder at the point it is ready for extraction, reflecting whether it is fully dried or still slightly moist.
Assessment of how uniform the powder is after preparation, recorded as a material property relevant to downstream extraction reproducibility.
Short description of how the prepared powder is stored before extraction, such as sealed_container, desiccated, refrigerated, or ambient. This is an intrinsic handling status of the material entity.

Approximate fraction of original dried plant mass retained as prepared powder after cleaning and milling, expressed as a fraction or percentage if tracked. Typical values are between 0 and 1 when stored as fraction.
Internal inventory or sample identifier for the prepared powder aliquot, using a stable string example such as 'PP-2024-05'. This is the material-level ID for the prepared entity.

extract_bioactive_compounds.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only extraction-operation metadata: solvent identity, solvent composition, extraction technique, ratio, time, temperature, agitation, cycles, and a simple extract quality/yield indicator. These fields describe how the prepared powder was transformed into crude extract. I excluded properties of the prepared powder itself because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded crude extract properties such as composition profiles or file-like outputs because those belong to the downstream Entity/Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating generic identifiers already generated elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Extraction approach used to enrich phytochemical constituents from the prepared plant powder, recorded at the point of operation. Examples include maceration, sonication, soxhlet, reflux, or accelerated_solvent_extraction.
Primary solvent used for extraction, recorded as the solvent applied to the plant powder during this process (for example, methanol, ethanol, water, ethyl_acetate).

Percentage of the primary solvent in the extraction mixture, measured at preparation of the extraction solvent if a mixture was used. Use 100 when a single solvent is used; typical range is 0 to 100 percent.
Mass-to-volume or mass-to-mass ratio used for extraction of the prepared powder, recorded as the operating ratio at the process step (for example, 1:10 w/v).

Temperature during extraction, in degrees Celsius, measured or set while the prepared powder was in contact with the solvent. Typical values range from ambient temperature to about 100 C depending on method.
Total extraction time, in hours, measured from start to end of solvent contact for this process. Typical values range from minutes to multiple hours depending on method.
Agitation or shaking speed applied during extraction, in revolutions per minute, if the method used mixing or shaking. Record the instrument setting used during the extraction interval.
Number of repeated extraction cycles performed on the same prepared powder batch, counted at process completion. Use 1 if extraction was performed once without repetition.
Approximate crude extract yield as a percentage of starting powder mass, calculated at the end of extraction. Typical values may range from 0 to 50 percent depending on plant and solvent.
Simple quality indicator for the extraction operation, such as complete, partial, or failed, recorded after the solvent extraction step is finished.

crude_plant_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the crude extract as a material: what it is, its physical state, concentration/solvent context, and storage/provenance details needed to hand it off to chromatography. I excluded extraction protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded chromatographic measurement settings, chromatogram file properties, and downstream separation outputs because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided reusing source-material identifiers already established elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name or internal label for the crude plant extract material, such as 'methanolic crude extract' or a lab inventory label. This identifies the extract entity used for downstream separation.
Residual or primary solvent associated with the crude extract at the time it enters downstream handling, for example methanol, ethanol, water, or ethyl_acetate.
Physical state of the crude extract entity at handoff to downstream processing, such as liquid, semisolid, or dried_residue.

Measured or prepared concentration of the crude extract solution, in milligrams per milliliter, if the extract is handled as a solution before chromatography. Typical values depend on assay or injection needs and may range from low single digits upward.
Mass of dried crude extract residue, in milligrams, when the extract is evaporated or lyophilized and tracked as a material quantity for downstream separation.
Temperature at which the crude extract is stored before downstream separation, in degrees Celsius. Record the temperature used for preserving the extract entity, such as -20 C or 4 C.
Container type used to store the crude extract, such as vial, amber_bottle, tube, or flask. Record the material container as stored before chromatography.
Internal batch identifier for the crude extract material, using a stable string example such as 'CE-001'. This identifies the extract lot handed to downstream separation.
Qualitative assessment of how crude or clean the extract appears before separation, recorded as an intrinsic material-quality description such as crude, partially_cleaned, or enriched.

chromatographic_separation.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included instrument- and session-level configuration fields for the LC/HPLC measurement: platform type, manufacturer/model/serial, column and mobile-phase setup, flow and gradient settings, injection volume, run timing, detector mode, and operator-controlled acquisition conditions. These describe the active measurement configuration and the instrument used to produce the chromatographic readout. I excluded file-format and trace properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node, and I excluded sample properties or fraction identities because those belong to upstream Entity/Process or downstream Process/Entity nodes. I also avoided repeating generic identifiers already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Chromatography system used for the measurement session, recorded as LC or HPLC at the point of acquisition. This describes the capture modality, not the sample or output file.
Manufacturer of the chromatography instrument used in this capture session, such as Agilent, Shimadzu, Waters, or Thermo Fisher.
Model name or number of the chromatography instrument used for separation capture, for example '1260 Infinity II'.
Serial number of the chromatography instrument used in this capture session, recorded as a stable string identifier such as 'SN-12345'.
Chromatographic column chemistry used during the run, recorded at the time of acquisition. Examples include C18, C8, phenyl, or normal_phase.
Physical dimensions of the chromatographic column used for capture, such as length x internal_diameter, recorded in millimeters when available (for example, '150 x 4.6 mm').
Solvent system used during chromatographic separation, recorded as the active mobile-phase composition at acquisition time (for example, water_acetonitrile with 0.1 percent formic acid).

Mobile-phase flow rate used during the chromatographic run, in milliliters per minute, measured or set during acquisition. Typical values are often between 0.1 and 2.0 mL/min depending on the column and method.
Volume of crude extract injected into the chromatography system for this capture session, in microliters. Typical values may range from 1 to 100 uL depending on method and column scale.
Total chromatographic run time, in minutes, measured from injection to final elution for the capture session. Typical values can range from a few minutes to over an hour.
Detector mode used to acquire the chromatographic signal, such as uv_vis, photodiode_array, fluorescence, or ms_detector, recorded as part of the capture configuration.
Detection wavelength used for UV/Vis-based chromatographic acquisition, in nanometers, recorded if the detector was wavelength-specific. Typical values may range from 190 to 800 nm.
Temperature of the chromatographic column during acquisition, in degrees Celsius, measured or set for the run. Typical values often range from ambient to about 60 C.
Operator-assessed quality indicator for the chromatography capture session, such as acceptable, noisy, or failed, recorded immediately after acquisition.

chromatogram_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-data artefact fields: file format, file size, dimensionality, acquisition trace characteristics, storage location, and technical quality metrics. These describe the chromatogram as a raw output of the capture step rather than the instrument settings or the chemical interpretation. I excluded chromatography configuration fields because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded fractionation or compound identity because those belong to downstream Process/Entity nodes. I also avoided repeating any generic identifiers already generated elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw chromatogram file produced by the capture system, for example 'sample01_chromatogram.raw' or 'run_12.d'. Record the exact file label used in storage.
Technical file format of the chromatogram signal, recorded as the raw or exported acquisition format at the point of storage. Examples include vendor_raw, cdf, mzml, or txt.
Size of the raw chromatogram file in bytes, measured at the time the signal file is stored or exported. This is a technical property of the data artefact.
Number of retention-time points or scans in the chromatogram signal, describing the raw trace dimensionality for the acquired run.
Number of detector channels recorded in the chromatogram file, such as a single UV channel or multiple wavelength channels.

Time interval between consecutive chromatographic data points, in seconds, measured for the raw signal acquisition. Typical values are often fractions of a second to several seconds depending on instrument settings.
Technical signal-to-noise ratio estimated for the raw chromatogram, recorded as a quality metric for the acquired trace. Use the value reported by the instrument or processing software if available.
Qualitative indicator of baseline stability in the raw chromatogram, recorded as a technical quality flag after acquisition. This reflects trace quality, not scientific interpretation.
Path, URI, or repository location where the raw chromatogram file is stored, for example a local path or object-store URL such as 's3://bucket/run12.raw'.
Integrity checksum for the chromatogram file, such as an MD5 or SHA hash string, used to verify that the raw signal file has not been altered.

fractionate_peaks.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only peak-fractionation operation details: fractionation mode, peak selection criteria, collection window settings, number of fractions, pooling strategy, and a simple fractionation quality indicator. These fields describe how the chromatogram signal was transformed into enriched fractions. I excluded chromatogram file properties and signal quality because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting fraction’s intrinsic properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided duplicating any already-generated fields from earlier nodes.

md_schema.descr: Mode used to isolate chromatographic peaks into fractions, recorded at the point of processing. Examples include manual_collection, automated_collection, or computational_segmentation.
Rule used to decide which chromatographic peaks were collected or segmented for downstream isolation, such as intensity_threshold, retention_window, or predefined_peak_list.
Retention-time window used for collecting or segmenting each fraction, in minutes, measured on the chromatographic time axis. Typical values depend on peak width and method resolution.
Total number of enriched fractions obtained from the chromatogram during this processing step, counted after peak collection or segmentation.
Strategy used to combine collected fractions, if applicable, such as single_peak, adjacent_peaks, or replicate_pooling. Record the actual pooling logic used in this process.
Temperature during fraction collection or handling, in degrees Celsius, measured while the fractions were being gathered or transferred. Typical values may be ambient or chilled conditions.
Total time required to complete peak fractionation, in minutes, measured from the start of collection or segmentation to completion.
Approximate percent of chromatographic material recovered into enriched fractions relative to the starting chromatogram load or collected peak mass, calculated at process completion.
Operator- or software-assessed quality indicator for the fractionation step, such as complete, partial, or failed, recorded after fractions are generated.

isolated_compound_fraction.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic material properties of the isolated fraction: fraction identity, composition/enrichment, amount, physical state, purity-level summaries, and storage conditions needed for later spectroscopy and bioactivity testing. I excluded the fractionation protocol itself because that belongs to the upstream Process node, and I excluded spectroscopic settings, spectra file properties, or assay conditions because those belong downstream. I also avoided reusing sample identifiers already generated at earlier Entity levels and kept the fields focused on what the fraction is rather than what will be done to it.

md_schema.descr: Name or internal label for the isolated compound fraction, such as a fraction number, peak label, or lab inventory name. This identifies the enriched material entity entering structural and functional analysis.
Identifier of the chromatographic peak or peak group from which this fraction originated, using the peak label reported by the fractionation step. Example format: 'P3' or 'peak_12'.

Qualitative assessment of how enriched the fraction is for candidate bioactive compound(s), recorded as an intrinsic material property after isolation. Examples include enriched, partially_enriched, or mixed.

Mass of the isolated fraction, in milligrams, measured after collection and any concentration or drying step. Typical values may range from sub-milligram to hundreds of milligrams depending on the separation scale.
Volume of the isolated fraction, in milliliters, if the fraction is retained as a liquid. Typical values depend on elution and collection scale.
Physical state of the isolated fraction at the time it is handed off for spectroscopy or assay, such as liquid, semisolid, or dried_residue.

Approximate purity estimate for the isolated fraction, expressed as a percentage if assessed by chromatography or related purity check. Typical values range from low purity mixtures to near-pure isolates.
Storage condition applied to the isolated fraction before downstream structural or functional analysis, such as refrigerated, frozen, desiccated, or ambient.
Internal inventory or sample identifier for the isolated fraction aliquot, using a stable string example such as 'IF-014'. This is the material-level ID for the fraction entity.
Estimated number of candidate bioactive compounds present in the fraction, recorded as an intrinsic compositional summary for the isolated material. Use 1 if a single dominant candidate is expected.

spectroscopic_measurement.reasoning: This is still a Capture node, so I kept only spectroscopy-session fields that do not collide with fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I removed instrument_manufacturer, instrument_model, instrument_serial_number, and capture_session_quality because they were flagged as duplicates across steps. I retained modality-specific acquisition settings that remain within this node’s scope: spectroscopy technique, sample preparation state, solvent/matrix, spectral range, resolution, scan count, acquisition mode, ionization source, and observed nucleus. These describe the configured measurement session without duplicating upstream or previously generated metadata.

md_schema.descr: Spectroscopic modality used in the measurement session, recorded at acquisition time. Examples include NMR, MS, IR, and UV-Vis.

Physical state of the isolated fraction when introduced into the spectrometer, such as solution, solid, pellet, or film. This describes the configured measurement sample state, not the fraction itself.
Solvent or matrix used to prepare the isolated fraction for spectroscopy, if applicable, such as CDCl3, DMSO-d6, methanol, or KBr.
Acquisition range used during the spectroscopy session, expressed as the active spectral window or m/z range depending on technique. Record the configured range at measurement time.
Instrument resolution or equivalent acquisition setting used for the spectroscopic run, recorded as configured on the instrument. Typical numeric meaning depends on the modality.
Number of scans, transients, or accumulations acquired for the spectroscopy measurement, depending on modality. Record the value set or achieved during acquisition.
Mode of spectroscopic acquisition used for the session, such as routine, high_resolution, tandem_ms, proton_nmr, carbon_nmr, or scan_based depending on modality.
Ionization source used for mass spectrometry capture, if MS was the modality, such as ESI, APCI, MALDI, or EI. Record only when applicable to the measurement session.
Nucleus observed for NMR spectroscopy, if NMR was the modality, such as 1H, 13C, or 15N. Record the active nucleus configured for the run.

spectral_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept only raw spectral artefact fields and removed all fields colliding with prior DAG steps as reported by the user. I excluded file_name, file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_location, signal_checksum, and signal_to_noise_ratio because they have already been generated elsewhere in the DAG. I also avoided capture settings and downstream interpretation. The remaining fields describe the raw spectral file’s dimensionality and axis characteristics without duplicating prior metadata.

md_schema.descr: Number of acquired spectral points, datapoints, or channels in the raw spectrum, describing the dimensionality of the signal artefact.
Observed axis range of the raw spectrum, such as chemical shift range for NMR or m/z range for MS, recorded as stored in the signal file.
Effective resolution or point spacing of the raw spectral signal, recorded as a technical characteristic of the data artefact. The exact meaning depends on modality.
Whether a baseline correction has already been applied to the stored spectral artefact. For a raw signal, this should usually be false unless the file is an uncollapsed acquisition export.

interpret_structure.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the interpretation workflow and its configurable parameters: analysis approach, software, version/repository, reference database, key criteria, confidence threshold, and a derived quality indicator. I excluded raw spectral file properties and acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream Signal/Capture nodes, and I excluded the final compound identity itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided any field ids already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including generic file- and signal-level ids that were flagged as collisions, and kept the scope strictly on how the spectral data were interpreted.

md_schema.descr: Method used to interpret spectral features into a chemical structure assignment, recorded at the processing step. Examples include manual_annotation, database_matching, rule_based_assignment, or hybrid_workflow.
Software used to perform or assist with structure interpretation, such as a cheminformatics or spectral analysis package. Record the software name used for this process step.
Version of the analysis software used for structure interpretation, recorded as the exact release used in the workflow.
Repository, package source, or project location for the analysis software when applicable, such as a GitHub URL, PyPI package name, or vendor repository reference.
Reference database or spectral library used for matching and structure assignment, such as HMDB, MassBank, NIST, or an in-house library.

Key criteria applied during spectral interpretation, such as exact_mass_match, fragment_pattern_match, chemical_shift_match, or combination_of_features. Record the rule set used to support the assignment.

Minimum confidence score or acceptance threshold required to report a structure assignment from the spectral interpretation step. Record the cutoff used, typically as a fraction between 0 and 1 or a percentage.

Broad structural class inferred from the spectra, such as flavonoid, alkaloid, terpenoid, phenolic_acid, or steroid. This is an intermediate interpretation output used before final compound identity reporting.
Simple quality indicator for the structure-interpretation step, such as supported, ambiguous, or failed, recorded after the analysis is complete.

structure_assignment.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed structure-result fields: assigned compound identity, structural class, formula-related outputs, identifiers, confidence, evidence basis, and output dimensionality/quality. I excluded raw spectral or capture parameters because those belong upstream, and I avoided repeating any field ids already used in prior nodes, especially generic software, file, and signal fields that were previously generated. The fields here describe the computed identification product produced from interpretation, not the underlying spectra or measurement settings.

md_schema.descr: Computed or assigned chemical name of the isolated compound, reported as the final structure identification produced by the interpretation workflow. Use the accepted name if known (for example, 'quercetin').
Standard chemical identifier for the assigned structure, such as a PubChem CID, ChEBI ID, InChIKey, or other stable reference string. Example format: 'InChIKey=XYZ...'.
Broad chemical class assigned to the compound as part of the computed structural result, such as flavonoid, alkaloid, terpenoid, phenolic_acid, or steroid.
Computed molecular formula of the assigned compound, recorded as an elemental formula string such as C15H10O7 when available from the structure assignment.

Calculated exact monoisotopic mass of the assigned structure, in daltons, derived from the computed structure assignment. Typical values depend on the compound and are usually reported to several decimal places.

Numerical confidence score for the structure assignment, recorded as the software- or analyst-reported confidence in the computed identification. Use a scale specified by the analysis workflow if available, commonly 0 to 1.
Primary evidence supporting the computed structure assignment, such as ms_fragmentation, nmr_pattern, database_match, or combined_evidence. Record the basis used to reach the final identification.
Whether stereochemical configuration was assigned as part of the computed structural identification, recorded as true when absolute or relative stereochemistry was resolved.
Overall status of the structure assignment result, such as confirmed, tentative, or unresolved, reflecting the final derivative quality of the computed identification.

prepare_cell_assay.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only assay-preparation operations: cell line choice, culture format, passage and seeding settings, treatment design, controls, incubation time, and assay-readiness quality. These fields describe how the cell assay was prepared and exposed to the isolated compound fraction. I excluded properties of the isolated fraction itself because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded measured bioactivity outputs because those belong to the downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided field ids that would collide with earlier nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the cell line or primary cell type prepared for the assay, recorded at the preparation step. Examples include RAW 264.7, THP-1, or HaCaT.
Culture format used for the assay preparation, such as adherent, suspension, co_culture, or primary_cells. Record the format actively prepared for bioactivity testing.
Passage number of the cells at the time the assay was prepared, recorded as the culture passage used for treatment. Typical values are integer passage counts.
Number of cells seeded per well, in cells per well, for the prepared assay plate. Typical values range from thousands to hundreds of thousands depending on cell type and plate format.
Microplate format used for the cell assay preparation, such as 6_well, 24_well, 48_well, or 96_well. Record the plate type into which cells were seeded.

Final concentration of the isolated compound fraction applied to the cells, in micromolar or micrograms per milliliter as defined by the workflow. Record the treatment concentration used during assay preparation.
Duration of compound exposure during assay preparation, in hours, measured from the start of treatment until the end of incubation before readout.
Whether a vehicle control was included in the assay preparation to match the compound solvent background. Record true if a control solvent condition was prepared.
Whether a positive control compound or condition was included in the assay preparation to validate the response. Record true if a known active control was prepared alongside test wells.
Incubation temperature used during cell culture preparation and compound treatment, in degrees Celsius. Typical values for mammalian cell assays are around 37 C.
Carbon dioxide concentration used during cell culture incubation, expressed as percent CO2 in the incubator atmosphere. Typical mammalian cell culture values are around 5 percent.
Overall quality indicator for the cell-assay preparation step, such as ready, contaminated, or failed, recorded after setup but before measurement.

assay_cell_culture.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the assay cell culture and removed the collided cell_line_name field noted by the user. The remaining fields describe the biological origin, culture characteristics, authentication/contamination status, and stock provenance of the living cell system. I excluded preparation conditions and all measurement outputs because those belong to upstream Process or downstream Capture/Signal nodes, not the entity itself. I also avoided repeating any other previously generated identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Broad category of the cell system, such as macrophage, epithelial, fibroblast, or primary_immune_cell. This describes the intrinsic biology of the assay entity.
Species from which the assay cell culture was derived, such as human, mouse, rat, or other mammalian origin. Record the biological source of the living cell system.
Original tissue or organ source of the cell culture, if known, such as blood, liver, lung, or skin. This is an intrinsic provenance property of the cell entity.
Whether the cell culture has been authenticated or verified, recorded as part of the biological entity characterization. Use verified, unverified, or mixed_status if applicable.
Whether the living cell system was confirmed free of mycoplasma contamination at the time it was used or stored. Record true when contamination testing was negative.

Growth medium used as the routine maintenance medium for the living cell system, such as DMEM, RPMI-1640, or MEM. This describes the entity's standard culture environment, not the assay treatment conditions.
Typical serum percentage used for routine maintenance of the cell culture, expressed as percent serum in the growth medium. Typical values often range from 5 to 20 percent.
Inventory or stock identifier for the cryopreserved cell aliquot used to establish the assay culture, such as 'CELL-STOCK-07'. This identifies the biological stock entity.
Short summary of the passage history of the cell stock or culture, such as early passage, mid passage, or high passage. This captures an intrinsic provenance/age characteristic of the entity.

cellular_bioactivity_capture.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw artefact fields for the cellular assay readout: file name, format, size, dimensions, channel count, storage location, checksums, and technical quality measures. I excluded capture-session fields, including the colliding plate_format, because those belong to the upstream Capture node and must not repeat. I also excluded assay interpretation and derived metrics because those belong downstream. The fields here describe the measured data file itself and its technical characteristics for reuse and QC.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw cellular bioactivity readout file produced by the capture system, for example 'assay01_readout.csv' or 'image_12.tif'. Record the exact file label used in storage.
Technical file format of the cellular bioactivity signal, recorded as the raw or exported acquisition format at the point of storage. Examples include csv, tiff, png, vendor_raw, or txt.
Size of the raw cellular bioactivity file in bytes, measured at the time the signal file is stored or exported. This is a technical property of the data artefact.
Number of measurement points, wells, frames, or samples recorded in the raw cellular assay signal, describing the dimensionality of the artefact.
Number of readout channels present in the signal file, such as multiple fluorescence channels or reporter channels.
Path, URI, or repository location where the raw cellular bioactivity file is stored, for example a local path or object-store URL such as 's3://bucket/assay01.csv'.
Integrity checksum for the cellular bioactivity file, such as an MD5 or SHA hash string, used to verify that the raw signal file has not been altered.

Technical signal-to-noise ratio estimated for the raw cellular assay readout, recorded as a quality metric for the acquired trace or image signal. Use the value reported by the instrument or export software if available.
Percent of wells or imaging field area successfully captured in the raw assay signal, recorded as a technical completeness measure for the data artefact. Typical values range from 0 to 100 percent.
Qualitative quality flag for the raw cellular bioactivity signal, such as good, noisy, saturated, or failed, recorded for the data artefact rather than the capture session.

bioactivity_signal.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only bioactivity-analysis operation parameters: normalization, background correction, replicate aggregation, response metric type, dose-response model, statistical test, and a process-level quality status. I removed the software identity fields because the user flagged analysis_software_name/version/repository as already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and those would otherwise collide. I also excluded raw assay file properties and capture settings because they belong upstream, and excluded final quantified outputs because those belong downstream to the Derivative node.

md_schema.descr: Method used to normalize raw cellular assay responses before metric calculation, recorded at the processing step. Examples include percent_of_control, z_score, baseline_subtraction, or none.
Approach used to correct background or blank signal in the assay data, such as mean_blank_subtraction or local_background_subtraction. Record the actual correction applied during analysis.
Rule used to combine replicate wells or fields before downstream metric derivation, such as mean, median, or trimmed_mean.
Primary bioactivity response metric calculated from the raw assay data, such as viability_percent, reporter_activity, oxidative_stress_reduction, or cytokine_suppression.

Mathematical model used to fit a concentration-response relationship, if the analysis included multiple doses. Examples include four_parameter_logistic, hill_equation, or none when a single dose was analyzed.
Statistical test applied during bioactivity analysis, if any, such as t_test, anova, or nonparametric_test. Record the main test used to support comparisons.
Overall quality indicator for the bioactivity analysis step, such as supported, ambiguous, or failed, recorded after normalization and metric derivation are complete.

analyze_bioactivity.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed result fields for the analyzed bioactivity output: final antioxidant and anti-inflammatory metrics, effect direction, potency summary, comparison to reference, confidence, and result quality. I excluded normalization, background correction, replicate aggregation, statistical test, and analysis quality fields because the user flagged those as already generated elsewhere; those belong to the upstream analysis Process node and must not be repeated. I also excluded raw assay properties and capture settings because those belong to Signal/Capture nodes. The fields here describe the derived comparative bioactivity product itself, suitable for downstream integration into the nutraceutical table.

md_schema.descr: Final derived antioxidant activity value computed from the analyzed assay data, reported in the workflow's chosen unit or scale (for example, percent inhibition, trolox equivalents, or index score). Record the value representing antioxidant effect after all analysis steps.

Final derived anti-inflammatory activity value computed from the analyzed assay data, reported in the workflow's chosen unit or scale (for example, percent suppression or index score). Record the value representing anti-inflammatory effect after all analysis steps.

Overall direction of the derived bioactivity result, indicating whether the compound fraction increased or decreased the relevant readout relative to the reference. Use this to summarize whether the effect is beneficial in the assay context.
Single summary potency metric derived from the bioactivity analysis, such as IC50, EC50, or an inhibition index, if a dose-response or comparative potency estimate was generated.

Outcome of the comparison between the tested fraction and the selected reference, such as stronger_than_control, similar_to_control, or weaker_than_control. This is a derived result summary, not the reference type itself.

Numeric confidence score for the derived bioactivity result, recorded as the analytical confidence in the final computed metrics. Use the workflow's native confidence scale if available, commonly 0 to 1.
Overall status of the derived bioactivity metrics, such as confirmed, tentative, or unresolved, recorded after analysis is complete.
Short free-text notes describing any caveats, outliers, or assay-specific interpretation remarks associated with the derived bioactivity result.

bioactivity_metrics.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only computed bioactivity-result descriptors that do not collide with already_generated fields. I retained output-scale, context, ranking, hit-calling, uncertainty, and result-status metadata, but removed the colliding metric-value and confidence field ids flagged by the user. I also stayed clear of process settings and raw signal properties because those belong upstream. The remaining fields describe the derived comparison outcome for the compound fraction, not how the assay was performed.

md_schema.descr: Units or reporting scale used for the derived bioactivity values, such as percent, trolox_equivalent, arbitrary_units, or fold_change. Record the scale used for the derived metrics if shared.

Context of the derived bioactivity values, such as concentration tested, reference control basis, or assay timepoint, used to interpret the computed metrics. Provide a compact descriptor like '10 uM vs vehicle control'.

Uncertainty or error estimate attached to the derived bioactivity values, such as standard deviation, standard error, or confidence interval half-width. Record the numeric magnitude in the same units as the primary value when possible.
Relative ranking of the tested compound fraction against other fractions or standards for the same bioactivity readout, such as top_hit, moderate_hit, or low_hit.
Binary or categorical hit-call for the derived bioactivity outcome, indicating whether the fraction meets the workflow's activity criterion.
Optional combined score summarizing antioxidant and anti-inflammatory performance into a single derivative measure, if the workflow computes one. Use the scale defined by the analysis pipeline.
Overall status of the derived bioactivity result, such as confirmed, tentative, or unresolved, recorded after metric calculation is complete.
Short composite label summarizing the derived bioactivity outcome, such as 'strong_antioxidant_and_anti_inflammatory' or 'moderate_activity'. This is a human-readable summary of the computed result.
Free-text note describing any important comparison caveat for the derived bioactivity result, such as comparator choice, assay limitations, or mixed endpoint behavior.

integrate_nutraceutical_results.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only integration-operation fields describing how structural assignments and bioactivity metrics are combined into a unified nutraceutical analysis. I focused on integration logic, weighting/priority rules, evidence requirements, standardization/claim-support categories, software used for the integration, and an overall integration quality indicator. I excluded the already-derived structure and bioactivity result values because those belong to the upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded raw signal/capture details because those belong much earlier in the DAG. I also avoided all colliding field ids previously generated, including the specific activity-value and confidence-score identifiers flagged by the user.

md_schema.descr: Method used to combine structural assignments and bioactivity metrics into a unified nutraceutical interpretation, recorded at the processing step. Examples include rule_based_merge, weighted_score_fusion, expert_curation, or statistical_integration.
Software or pipeline used to integrate structure and bioactivity results into the unified analysis, such as a statistics package, workflow script, or curation tool.
Version of the integration software or pipeline used for nutraceutical result synthesis, recorded as the exact release used in the workflow.
Repository, package source, or project location for the integration software when applicable, such as a GitHub URL, package name, or internal repository reference.

Relative weights or priorities assigned to structure assignment versus bioactivity evidence when producing the unified interpretation, recorded as a compact description or numeric vector if applicable.
Minimum evidence required for a compound fraction to be included in the unified nutraceutical analysis, such as confirmed_structure plus confirmed_bioactivity or analogous criteria.
Level of support the integrated result provides for nutraceutical standardization, such as high, moderate, or low, assessed at the end of the integration step.
Category of health-benefit claim support derived from the integrated analysis, such as antioxidant_support, anti_inflammatory_support, dual_support, or insufficient_support.
Optional composite score summarizing the combined structural and bioactivity evidence for nutraceutical decision-making, using the scale defined by the workflow.
Overall quality indicator for the integration step, such as supported, ambiguous, or failed, recorded after combining structure and bioactivity evidence.

nutraceutical_metadata_table.reasoning: This is the final Derivative node, so I included only table-level outputs needed to use the integrated result as a reusable metadata table: row/table identifier, linked source fraction/structure/result references, summary columns for identity and evidence traceability, nutraceutical classification, and table completeness/quality. I excluded upstream process, capture, and signal details because this node is the consolidated derived table, not the individual measurements or transformations. I also avoided repeating any field ids already generated elsewhere, especially the activity, software, and confidence identifiers that collided in earlier steps. The fields here are meant to make the integrated table searchable, auditable, and useful for standardized nutraceutical development and claims support.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for a single row in the nutraceutical metadata table, using a stable string such as 'ROW-0001'. This identifies the integrated record within the final derived table.
Identifier of the isolated compound fraction represented in this table row, linking the integrated record back to the upstream fraction entity (for example, a fraction label or inventory ID).
Identifier of the structure-assignment result associated with this table row, linking the record to the computed compound identity output.
Identifier of the bioactivity-derived result associated with this table row, linking the record to the computed antioxidant and anti-inflammatory outcome.

Concise human-readable summary of the compound identity included in the final table, such as accepted compound name plus class or key synonym. This is the table-ready identity field for downstream use.
Short summary of the chromatographic provenance for the integrated record, such as peak label, retention window, or fraction source used to trace the compound back to the separation step.
Compact summary of the spectral assignment evidence included in the table, such as NMR/MS/IR support or database match notation. This is a table-level synopsis rather than the raw spectra.

Compact summary of the integrated bioactivity outcome, such as antioxidant and anti-inflammatory response descriptors or hit-call status. This summarizes the derivative bioactivity result for table use.

Categorical classification of the integrated record for nutraceutical development, such as candidate, prioritized_candidate, standardization_reference, or excluded. Record the workflow's final utility category.
Whether the integrated table row is considered supportive of a health-benefit claim in the workflow context. Use true only when the combined evidence satisfies the project's claim-support criteria.
Overall completeness or curation status of the final table row, such as complete, partial, or needs_review, assessed after integration of all upstream evidence.
